   147	/-! ## §1. The two hypotheses, named -/
   148	
   149	/-- **Every finite subset lies in a single affine open** — the action-free,
   150	scheme-level form of the EGA II 4.5.4 orbit hypothesis.
   151	
   152	`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` (`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`) is
   153	stated *about an action*, so a consumer cannot discharge it before knowing which
   154	action it will face. This form is a property of the scheme alone, and §2 shows it
   155	implies the action form for **every** semilinear action of a finite Galois group.
   156	That is what lets the antecedent of §4 be stated without mentioning the Galois
   157	level, which is chosen inside the proof.
   158	
   159	True for quasi-projective schemes (finite point sets of a quasi-projective scheme
   160	lie in an affine open). Mathlib `v4.31` has no quasi-projectivity vocabulary at
   161	this pin, which is why the hypothesis is carried in this elementary form rather
   162	than derived. -/
   163	def FiniteInAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop :=
   164	  ∀ s : Set X, s.Finite → ∃ U : X.affineOpens, s ⊆ U.1
   165	
   166	/-- **The pointed Picard theorem**: FGA/Kleiman representability of the relative
   167	Picard functor, for curves that *have* a rational point, uniformly in the base
   168	field, together with quasi-projectivity of the representing scheme.
   169	
   170	This is the campaign's target, written as a closed proposition. Three things about
   171	its shape are deliberate, and a fourth is deliberately **absent**.
   172	
   173	* It quantifies over **all** base fields `K`, not just over `k`. That is
   174	  essential and it is not a strengthening in any useful sense: §4 applies it at a
   175	  finite Galois extension of `k` chosen by the curve, so a version fixed at `k`
   176	  would not compose. Every formalisation route to FGA representability is uniform
   177	  in the base field anyway.
   178	* It is about `picSharp`, the **unsheafified** relative Picard functor — the object
   179	  the Milne–Kollár modules target (`I-0907`). No étale-sheafified representability
   180	  statement is needed on top of it; §3 of `Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean` supplies
   181	  the transport for free.
   182	* `FiniteInAffine X.left` is bundled rather than carried separately so that the
   183	  results below have **one** antecedent. The *property* is perfectly stateable
   184	  outside it — `HasGoodGaloisLevel` in §5 does exactly that, and §2 takes it as a
   185	  free-standing hypothesis. What cannot be stated outside is the **witness**: no
   186	  separate binder can name the scheme the antecedent itself produces. (An earlier
   187	  revision of this bullet said the property "cannot be stated outside it", which
   188	  two declarations in this same file refute.)
   189	* **`IsSeparated X.hom` is NOT a conjunct**, and carrying it would have
   190	  misreported the price of the reduction. It is *free* from the resulting `picEt`
   191	  representation by `isSeparated_of_representableBy_picEt`
   192	  (`Picard/PicEtSeparated.lean`) — Yoneda transports the `CommGrpCat`-valued
   193	  functor's group structure onto any representing scheme, and a group scheme over
   194	  a field is separated. That file's
   195	  `picEtClauseOne_of_picSharp_representableBy_locallyOfFiniteType` already says
   196	  in its own docstring that the form to hand the campaign asks "nothing about
   197	  separatedness". A first revision of this file bundled it anyway; a
   198	  fresh-context audit reproved every result with the conjunct deleted, so it is
   199	  deleted. The seam's clause (1) still *concludes* separatedness — it is
   200	  discharged, not dropped. -/
   201	def PointedPicSharpRep : Prop :=
   202	  ∀ {K : Type u} [Field K] (E : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))),
   203	    ∀ [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 E.hom] [IsProper E.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral E.hom],
   204	      Scheme.HasRationalPoint E →
   205	      ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)),
   206	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp E).RepresentableBy X) ∧
   207	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ FiniteInAffine X.left
   208	
   209	/-! ## §2. The scheme-level hypothesis implies the action-level one -/
   210	
   211	/-- **`FiniteInAffine` discharges `OrbitsInAffineOpen`, for every semilinear
   212	action of a finite Galois group.**
   213	
   214	The orbit of a point is the range of a map indexed by `L ≃ₐ[K] L`, which is finite
   215	because `L/K` is finite Galois (`Finite (L ≃ₐ[K] L)` by synthesis), so it is a
   216	finite subset and the hypothesis applies directly.
   217	
   218	Note where the finiteness of the group is consumed: only here. The quotient
   219	machinery downstream binds `[FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]` for its own
   220	reasons. -/
   221	theorem orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
   222	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
   223	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
   224	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   225	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (h : FiniteInAffine X) :
   226	    ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen where
   227	  exists_affineOpen x := by
   228	    obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
   229	      h (Set.range fun γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (ρ.act γ).hom.base x) (Set.finite_range _)
   230	    exact ⟨U, fun γ => hU ⟨γ, rfl⟩⟩
   231	
   232	/-! ## §3. `FiniteInAffine` is inhabited, and is not free
   233	
   234	Both directions are recorded as declarations rather than as docstring sentences,
   235	per `I-0838`: a hypothesis whose satisfiability is unmeasured is how a vacuous
   236	statement survives, and a hypothesis that is *free* would make the results below
   237	empty. -/
   238	
   239	/-- **Non-vacuity**: an affine scheme satisfies `FiniteInAffine`, with `⊤` as the
   240	affine open. So the antecedent of §4 is not asserting something about no scheme.
   241	
   242	This is the cheap witness, and it is the honest one to give: it is *not* a witness
   243	at a Picard scheme, and no such witness exists in this project. What it rules out
   244	is the failure mode where `FiniteInAffine` is unsatisfiable and the results below
   245	are vacuously true. -/
   246	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] : FiniteInAffine X :=
   247	  fun _ _ => ⟨⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩, fun _ _ => trivial⟩
   248	
   249	/-! ## §4. The reduction
   250	
   251	Clause (2) first, because it needs strictly less. -/
   252	
   253	/-- **Clause (2) of the seam, from the pointed antecedent alone.**
   254	
   255	No Galois level, no quotient, no orbit hypothesis, and the `FiniteInAffine`
   256	conjunct of the antecedent is discarded: given a section, the antecedent applies
   257	to `C` *itself*, and subcanonicity of the étale topology turns a representation
   258	into invertibility of the comparison map
   259	(`isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability`).
   260	
   261	So of the seam's two conjuncts, this one costs nothing beyond the pointed theorem.
   262	That is a sharper statement than the seam docstring's "clause (2) costs zero extra
   263	work", which was said relative to a `picSharp`-shaped endpoint over the *same*
   264	field; here it is said relative to the pointed antecedent, which is the thing
   265	actually being assumed. -/
   266	theorem seamClauseTwo_of_pointedPicSharpRep {k : Type u} [Field k]
   267	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   268	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
   269	    (H : PointedPicSharpRep.{u}) :
   270	    Scheme.HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C) := by
   271	  intro hpt
   272	  obtain ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩, -, -⟩ := H C hpt
   273	  exact isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability C rep
   274	
   275	/-- **Clause (1) of the seam, over an ARBITRARY field, from the pointed
   276	antecedent.** This is the theorem the file exists for.
   277	
   278	The proof is the composition the module docstring describes, and each step is a
   279	landed sorry-free theorem of a different lane:
   280	
   281	1. `exists_finiteGalois_level_hasRationalPoint_of_geometricallyIntegral` produces
   282	   a finite **Galois** `k''/k` and a rational point on `C_{k''}` — unconditionally,
   283	   from `[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1]` and `[GeometricallyIntegral]` alone. This
   284	   is the only step that uses `GeometricallyIntegral`.
   285	2. The antecedent, applied at `k''` to the base-changed curve (all three binders
   286	   are stable under field base change, by synthesis), gives a scheme representing
   287	   `picSharp (C_{k''})` with the two side conjuncts and `FiniteInAffine`.
   288	3. `picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` converts it to a `picEt`
   289	   representation — the same scheme, so `LocallyOfFiniteType` rides along.
   290	4. §2 turns `FiniteInAffine` into `OrbitsInAffineOpen` at the canonical semilinear
   291	   action `semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep`, which is the action the
   292	   descent step uses.
   293	5. `seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree` descends to `k`, discharging the
   294	   quotient and the covering sieve internally.
   295	
   296	The conclusion is over `k` with **no** section and **no** `k''` in sight, and no
   297	hypothesis of the theorem mentions a representation of `picEt C` — so this is not
   298	`P → P`, and it is not the refuted shape of `representableByRestrict_of_baseChange`
   299	(`I-1312`), which concluded about a `k'`-object. -/
   300	theorem seamClauseOne_of_pointedPicSharpRep {k : Type u} [Field k]
   301	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   302	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
   303	    (H : PointedPicSharpRep.{u}) :
   304	    ∃ Z : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
   305	      Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy Z) ∧
   306	        LocallyOfFiniteType Z.hom ∧ IsSeparated Z.hom := by
   307	  obtain ⟨k'', hfd, hgal, hpt⟩ :=
   308	    Scheme.exists_finiteGalois_level_hasRationalPoint_of_geometricallyIntegral C
   309	  letI := hfd
   310	  letI := hgal
   311	  obtain ⟨X', ⟨rep0⟩, hft, hfa⟩ := H (Scheme.baseChangeField C (k'' : Type u)) hpt
   312	  letI rep :=
   313	    picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport (Scheme.baseChangeField C (k'' : Type u)) rep0
   314	  letI := orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
   315	    (PicScheme.semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep) hfa
   316	  exact PicScheme.seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree rep hft
   317	
   318	/-- **The seam, verbatim, as the conclusion of an implication.**
   319	
   320	The conclusion is character-for-character the statement of
   321	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`, so a lane that proves `PointedPicSharpRep`
   322	closes the project's central `sorry` by `exact`. Stated as a named theorem rather
   323	than left to the reader to assemble, because "the two clauses are available
   324	separately" is not the same as "the seam follows", and the difference is exactly
   325	the kind of joint that goes unchecked. -/
   326	theorem fgaPicardRepresentability_of_pointedPicSharpRep {k : Type u} [Field k]
   327	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   328	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
   329	    (H : PointedPicSharpRep.{u}) :
   330	    (∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
   331	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
   332	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom)
   333	      ∧ (Scheme.HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)) :=
   334	  ⟨seamClauseOne_of_pointedPicSharpRep C H, seamClauseTwo_of_pointedPicSharpRep C H⟩
   335	
   336	/-! ## §5. The weakest antecedent clause (1) actually needs
   337	
   338	§4 states the reduction against `PointedPicSharpRep`, which is the shape a
   339	*campaign* delivers: uniform in the field, stated with a rational-point
   340	hypothesis. That is the right form for a hand-off, and it is deliberately
   341	stronger than the proof consumes. This section writes down what clause (1) really
   342	needs, because a reduction priced against an over-strong antecedent misreports
   343	what is left.
   344	
   345	Three things fall away, and each is a fact about the proof rather than a
   346	restatement.
   347	
   348	* **The uniformity in the field.** Only ONE extension is used. Not "all
   349	  fields", not even "all finite Galois levels of `k`" — a single good level
   350	  suffices, so the antecedent is an existential.
   351	* **The rational point.** It does not occur in `HasGoodGaloisLevel` at all. In §4
   352	  it is the *route* by which the level is produced (via
   353	  `exists_finiteGalois_level_hasRationalPoint_of_geometricallyIntegral`), but the
   354	  descent step never looks at it. A lane that can represent `picSharp` over some
   355	  finite Galois extension by any other means owes no section.
   356	* **`[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]` and `IsSeparated`.** The former is used in §4
   357	  *only* to produce the level, so with the level assumed it is not a binder here
   358	  — this theorem holds for a smooth proper `C` with no integrality hypothesis at
   359	  all. The latter is not an input in either form: it comes from the group
   360	  structure of the represented object (`PicEtSeparated`, consumed inside
   361	  `seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree`).
   362	
   363	**On the converse — and this paragraph is a CORRECTION of what stood here.** The
   364	first revision said the converse "fails even at the trivial extension `k' = k`",
   365	evidenced by `exact?` failing on
   366	`Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy Z)` from `(picEt C).RepresentableBy Z`,
   367	and gave as the reason that the `PicEtSubcanonical.lean` transport "runs
   368	`picSharp → picEt` only, because it is the sheafification unit". **The reason was
   369	false and the probe was inadequate** (fresh-context audit, reproduced here before
   370	accepting). The comparison is a *morphism*; once it is an iso,
   371	`RepresentableBy.ofIso` runs both ways, and
   372	
   373	  `converseOfIsIso : IsIso (picEtComparison C) → (picEt C).RepresentableBy Z →`
   374	  `  Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy Z)`
   375	
   376	is the three-line term below — the same term already landed inside
   377	`picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`), i.e. in this
   378	file's own import closure, which the withdrawn paragraph did not mention. And the
   379	hypothesis it needs is supplied by **clause (2) of this file's own antecedent**:
   380	under `PointedPicSharpRep`, `seamClauseTwo_of_pointedPicSharpRep` gives
   381	`IsIso (picEtComparison C)` at every curve *with a section*.
   382	
   383	So the honest statement is narrower than "not equivalent" and sharper than
   384	"equivalent": the two representability notions are **interderivable at every
   385	pointed curve**, and the gap is confined exactly to curves with **no** rational
   386	point — where `¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)` is Kleiman's pointless real conic,
   387	quoted in `Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean` and *not proved* in this project. That
   388	is still a genuine gap and this is still not a change of coordinates, but the
   389	reason is the pointless case, not the direction of the unit. Contrast
   390	`coverCompatibleEquiv_of_representableBy`
   391	(`Picard/PicEtDescentRepresentability.lean`), whose converse is unconditional. -/
   392	def HasGoodGaloisLevel {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   393	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] : Prop :=
   394	  ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k'),
   395	    ∃ (_ : FiniteDimensional k k') (_ : IsGalois k k')
   396	      (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k'))),
   397	      Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp (Scheme.baseChangeField C k')).RepresentableBy X) ∧

     9	/-!
    10	# Finite subsets in affine opens
    11	
    12	`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` is the action-free geometric condition behind the
    13	finite-Galois quotient construction: every finite subset of `X` lies in one
    14	affine open.  For a finite Galois extension, this immediately supplies
    15	`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` for every action on `X`.
    16	
    17	The property is stated independently of Picard data.  In particular, it is a
    18	conclusion to be proved for a representing scheme, not an additional field of
    19	the representability datum.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory
    27	open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
    30	
    31	/-- Every finite subset of a scheme is contained in a single affine open. -/
    32	def FiniteInAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop :=
    33	  ∀ s : Set X, s.Finite → ∃ U : X.affineOpens, s ⊆ U.1
    34	
    35	/-- An affine scheme satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
    36	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] :
    37	    FiniteInAffine X :=
    38	  fun _ _ ↦ ⟨⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩, fun _ _ ↦ trivial⟩
    39	
    40	/-- `FiniteInAffine` is invariant under isomorphism. -/
    41	theorem finiteInAffine_of_iso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ≅ Y)
    42	    (h : FiniteInAffine X) : FiniteInAffine Y := by
    43	  intro s hs
    44	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (e.hom.base ⁻¹' s)
    45	    (hs.preimage (TopCat.homeoOfIso ((Scheme.forgetToTop).mapIso e)).injective.injOn)
    46	  refine ⟨⟨e.hom ''ᵁ U.1, U.2.image_of_isOpenImmersion e.hom⟩, ?_⟩
    47	  intro y hy
    48	  exact ⟨e.inv.base y, hU (by simpa using hy), by simp⟩
    49	
    50	/-- `FiniteInAffine` descends along an affine morphism. -/
    51	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    52	    [IsAffineHom f] (h : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
    53	  intro s hs
    54	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (f.base '' s) (hs.image _)
    55	  exact ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1, U.2.preimage f⟩, fun x hx ↦ hU ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩⟩
    56	
    57	/-- An object affine over a field spectrum satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
    58	theorem finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom {k : Type u} [Field k]
    59	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsAffineHom X.hom] :
    60	    FiniteInAffine X.left :=
    61	  haveI := isAffine_of_isAffineHom X.hom
    62	  finiteInAffine_of_isAffine _
    63	
    64	/-- `FiniteInAffine` supplies the orbit condition for every finite-Galois
    65	semilinear action on the scheme. -/
    66	theorem orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
    67	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    68	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    69	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    70	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (h : FiniteInAffine X) :
    71	    rho.OrbitsInAffineOpen where
    72	  exists_affineOpen x := by
    73	    obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
    74	      h (Set.range fun gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L ↦ (rho.act gamma).hom.base x)
    75	        (Set.finite_range _)
    76	    exact ⟨U, fun gamma ↦ hU ⟨gamma, rfl⟩⟩
    77	
    78	end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

    12	/-!
    13	# Quasi-projectivity, as the vocabulary `FiniteInAffine` was standing in for
    14	
    15	`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`) says every finite
    16	subset of `X` lies in a single affine open.  It is the elementary, action-free form
    17	of the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis that the whole finite-Galois-quotient engine runs
    18	on, and up to now the project carried it **by hand**, with the same sentence
    19	written in three places: *"it holds for quasi-projective `X`, but mathlib has no
    20	quasi-projectivity vocabulary at this pin, so for the curve it must be supplied by
    21	hand"* (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`,
    22	`Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean`, `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).
    23	
    24	This file removes the hand: it derives `FiniteInAffine` from the project's
    25	finite-projective-space notion `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective`; projectivity is
    26	the closed-immersion special case.  The chain is
    27	
    28	  graded prime avoidance  ⟹  `FiniteInAffine (Proj 𝒜)`
    29	                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine ℙ(n; S)`   (affine morphism descent)
    30	                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine X` for `X` H-quasi-projective over `S`.
    31	
    32	## The two avoidance inputs
    33	
    34	The original deep input is the first step, and it is **absent from mathlib
    35	`v4.31`**: there is no *graded* prime avoidance.  Mathlib has
    36	`Ideal.subset_union_prime_finite` — a homogeneous ideal not contained in the union
    37	of finitely many primes is not contained in any one of them — but the element it
    38	produces is an arbitrary element of the ideal, while
    39	`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen` demands `f ∈ 𝒜 m` with `0 < m`.
    40	Getting a **homogeneous** avoiding element of **positive degree** is §1, and it is
    41	where the grading is consumed.
    42	
    43	For a closed immersion the final transport is cheap: `IsClosedImmersion →
    44	IsAffineHom`, and `IsAffineOpen.preimage` pulls affine opens back.  An open
    45	immersion needs a second prime-avoidance step: after placing the finite image in
    46	an affine open, `GaloisDescent.exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite` shrinks it to a
    47	basic open lying inside the immersion range.  The standard closed/open
    48	factorization then gives transport along every immersion.
    49	
    50	Thus graded avoidance is the new algebraic result in this file.  Open-immersion
    51	transport is the only additional substantive geometric step; its algebra is
    52	delegated to the already-landed finite prime-avoidance theorem.  The remaining
    53	H-quasi-projective and coproduct declarations are factorization and packaging.
    54	
    55	## What this does and does not buy
    56	
    57	It does **not** discharge the `FiniteInAffine` conjunct of
    58	`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep`.  That conjunct is about the **Picard scheme**, and
    59	nothing in this project produces an H-quasi-projective witness for the relevant
    60	Picard component.  Kleiman §5 `th:qpp&p` gives quasi-projectivity of `Pic^0`;
    61	formalizing and transporting that source theorem remains open.  What changes is the *kind* of thing
    62	that is open: the antecedent's last non-projection conjunct is now reducible to a
    63	standard geometric hypothesis with a standard proof, rather than an elementary
    64	condition invented here.  Stated as
    65	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isHQuasiProjective` in §3.
    66	
    67	It **does** discharge, unconditionally and for free, the orbit hypothesis of the
    68	Galois-descent engine at every projective scheme
    69	(`Scheme.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_isProjective`), which is what
    70	`Picard/GaloisQuotientNonVacuity.lean` had only for *affine* `X` and what the
    71	Albanese lane's `OrbitsInAffineOpen` had for no `X` at all.  Smooth proper
    72	geometrically integral curves **are** projective in this project
    73	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral`,
    74	`Picard/CurveProjectivity.lean`), so §3 fires at the curve itself with no
    75	hypothesis beyond its own binders.
    76	
    77	## What §5 is NOT: read this before consuming `PointedPicSharpRepProjective`
    78	
    79	§5 restates the seam's antecedent with `IsProjective` of the representing scheme in
    80	place of `FiniteInAffine`.  **That antecedent is refuted at the object it is about**,
    81	and the refutation is landed here as a theorem, not left as prose:
    82	`Scheme.not_isProjective_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover`.  Projectivity over a field
    83	forces `IsProper`, hence `UniversallyClosed`, hence — over the compact `Spec k` —
    84	`CompactSpace` (`Scheme.compactSpace_of_isProjective`); and the full Picard scheme is a
    85	**disjoint union over `deg ∈ ℤ`** (Kleiman §6 `ex:curves`), which is not quasi-compact.
    86	So `PointedPicSharpRepProjective` is not the standard hypothesis restated — it is
    87	strictly stronger and false at `Pic_{C/k}`.
    88	
    89	This is verbatim the trap `Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean` exists to record, "trap (c):
    90	a `P → Q` whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting", and it is caught by
    91	that file's own theorems.  Kleiman's `th:qpp&p` gives quasi-projectivity of `Pic^0`,
    92	not projectivity of the ambient scheme.  §5 therefore survives only as a
    93	*conditional* reduction with an explicitly refuted antecedent; §3 and §4, which do not
    94	mention the ambient Picard scheme, are unaffected.
    95	
    96	An earlier revision of this section said §5 states the seam "with no condition invented
    97	in this project anywhere in it".  Both halves were wrong: `Scheme.Hom.IsProjective` is
    98	project-local (`Picard/ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean`, mathlib `v4.31` has no
    99	morphism-level projectivity at all), as are `PicScheme.picSharp` and
   100	`Scheme.HasRationalPoint`; and the antecedent is not merely non-standard but refutable.
   101	The defensible statement is the narrow one: the *mathematical notion* is standard even
   102	though the Lean definition is ours.
   103	
   104	## Non-vacuity
   105	
   106	`FiniteInAffine` is satisfiable at an affine scheme with `⊤`
   107	(`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isAffine`, already landed) and that witness is
   108	*degenerate*: it says nothing about the projective case.  So the honest
   109	non-degeneracy evidence for §2 is what a fresh-context audit could **verify**, and it
   110	is at `Proj`: `Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) ℚ)` is nonempty (the point
   111	`V(X₀)`), and the hypotheses of `Scheme.exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem` are jointly
   112	satisfiable there, both checked by elaborating them at that named object.
   113	
   114	**What is NOT verified, stated because an earlier revision of this paragraph asserted
   115	it as the ground of non-degeneracy:** that `ℙ(n; S)` fails to be affine for `n` with at
   116	least two elements.  It is true, but it is proved nowhere in mathlib at this pin
   117	(no `¬ IsAffine` results at all) nor in this project, so
   118	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace` being a *non-affine* witness rests on prose.
   119	That earlier revision also claimed the caution "is recorded as
   120	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace`"; that theorem records no such thing — it has no
   121	`Nonempty` hypothesis and no non-affineness content.
   122	-/

   132	/-! ## §1. Graded prime avoidance
   133	
   134	The new algebraic input.  The open-immersion theorem in §2 is the other
   135	substantive geometric step, delegating its algebra to `StableAffineCover`.
   136	-/
   137	
   138	section GradedAvoidance
   139	
   140	variable {σ : Type*} {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A]
   141	variable (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜]
   142	
   143	/-- **A finite `inf` of homogeneous ideals is homogeneous.** Bookkeeping for the
   144	avoidance argument, which needs `I ⊓ ⨅_{i ≠ j} p i` to be homogeneous in order to
   145	extract a homogeneous element from it. -/
   146	theorem Ideal.IsHomogeneous.finsetInf {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (p : ι → Ideal A)
   147	    (h : ∀ i ∈ s, (p i).IsHomogeneous 𝒜) : (s.inf p).IsHomogeneous 𝒜 := by
   148	  classical
   149	  induction s using Finset.induction with
   150	  | empty =>
   151	      rw [Finset.inf_empty]
   152	      exact fun _ _ _ => Submodule.mem_top
   153	  | insert a t _ IH =>
   154	      rw [Finset.inf_insert]
   155	      exact fun i x hx =>
   156	        ⟨h a (Finset.mem_insert_self a t) i hx.1,
   157	          IH (fun j hj => h j (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hj)) i hx.2⟩
   158	
   159	/-- **Graded prime avoidance at a single relevant homogeneous prime.** If a
   160	homogeneous ideal `I` is not contained in a homogeneous prime `p`, and `p` does not
   161	contain the irrelevant ideal, then `I` has a homogeneous element of **strictly
   162	positive** degree outside `p`.
   163	
   164	Two separate uses of the grading, and it is worth naming both because the second is
   165	the one an ungraded intuition drops:
   166	
   167	* `I` homogeneous and `¬ I ≤ p` gives a homogeneous element of `I` outside `p` —
   168	  decompose a witness and note that if every component were in `p` so would the
   169	  witness be. Its degree is **not controlled** and may be `0`.
   170	* Relevance of `p` (`¬ 𝒜₊ ≤ p`) gives a homogeneous `g ∉ p` of positive degree, by
   171	  the same decomposition applied to a witness in the irrelevant ideal, whose
   172	  degree-`0` component is zero by definition.
   173	
   174	Then `f₀ * g` is homogeneous of degree `> 0`, lies in `I` (an ideal) and avoids `p`
   175	(a prime). Relevance is exactly what makes this possible: over a `p` containing
   176	`𝒜₊` — i.e. at a point *not* in `Proj` — every positive-degree homogeneous element
   177	lies in `p` and the conclusion is false. -/
   178	theorem exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem
   179	    {I p : Ideal A} [hp : p.IsPrime] (hI : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
   180	    (hrel : ¬ (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal ≤ p) (hIp : ¬ I ≤ p) :
   181	    ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ f ∈ I ∧ f ∉ p := by
   182	  classical

   208	/-- **Graded prime avoidance for an incomparable family** — the case with the

   210	
   211	Given finitely many pairwise-incomparable relevant homogeneous primes `q ∈ T`, none

   213	`I` of **positive** degree outside every one of them.
   214	
   215	The classical product/sum trick, with the grading forcing one extra step:
   216	
   217	* Incomparability makes `I ⊓ ⨅_{q' ∈ T, q' ≠ q} q'` not contained in `q` — if it
   218	  were, primality would put one of the factors inside `q`. So

   220	  `f q ∈ I` of positive degree `m q` that lies in every *other* member of `T` and

   223	  `M := ∏ m q` each `m q` divides `M`, and `F q := (f q) ^ (M / m q)` is homogeneous
   224	  of the **common** degree `M > 0`, still in `I` and with the same membership
   225	  pattern (a prime contains a power iff it contains the base).

   231	theorem exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem_of_antichain
   232	    (T : Finset (Ideal A)) (hp : ∀ q ∈ T, q.IsPrime)
   233	    (hph : ∀ q ∈ T, q.IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
   234	    (hrel : ∀ q ∈ T, ¬ (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal ≤ q)
   235	    (hanti : ∀ q ∈ T, ∀ q' ∈ T, q ≠ q' → ¬ q ≤ q')
   236	    {I : Ideal A} (hI : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜) (hIp : ∀ q ∈ T, ¬ I ≤ q)
   237	    (hM : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ f ∈ I) :
   238	    ∃ (M : ℕ) (h : A), 0 < M ∧ h ∈ 𝒜 M ∧ h ∈ I ∧ ∀ q ∈ T, h ∉ q := by
   239	  classical
   240	  rcases T.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | hne
   241	  · obtain ⟨m, f, hm, hfd, hfI⟩ := hM
   242	    exact ⟨m, f, hm, hfd, hfI, by simp⟩
   243	  -- Choose, for each `q ∈ T`, a homogeneous positive-degree element of
   244	  -- `I ⊓ ⨅_{q' ≠ q} q'` outside `q`.
   245	  have key : ∀ q ∈ T, ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧
   246	      f ∈ (I ⊓ (T.erase q).inf id) ∧ f ∉ q := by
   247	    intro q hq
   248	    haveI := hp q hq
   249	    refine exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem 𝒜 (I := I ⊓ (T.erase q).inf id) ?_ (hrel q hq) ?_
   250	    · exact fun i x hx =>
   251	        ⟨hI i hx.1,
   252	          Ideal.IsHomogeneous.finsetInf 𝒜 _ id
   253	            (fun q' hq' => hph q' (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hq')) i hx.2⟩
   254	    · intro hle
   255	      rcases (hp q hq).inf_le.mp hle with h | h
   256	      · exact hIp q hq h
   257	      · obtain ⟨q', hq', hq'le⟩ := (hp q hq).inf_le'.mp h
   258	        exact hanti q' (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hq') q hq
   259	          (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hq') hq'le
   260	  choose! m f hmpos hfdeg hfmem hfout using key
   261	  have hfI : ∀ q ∈ T, f q ∈ I := fun q hq => (hfmem q hq).1
   262	  have hfin : ∀ q ∈ T, ∀ q' ∈ T.erase q, f q ∈ q' := fun q hq q' hq' =>
   263	    Finset.inf_le (f := id) hq' (hfmem q hq).2
   264	  -- Equalise the degrees: `M := ∏ m q`, and `F q := (f q) ^ (M / m q)` has degree `M`.

   267	  have hquot : ∀ q ∈ T, 0 < M / m q := fun q hq =>
   268	    Nat.div_pos (Finset.single_le_prod' (fun i hi => hmpos i hi) hq) (hmpos q hq)
   269	  set F : Ideal A → A := fun q => (f q) ^ (M / m q) with hFdef
   270	  have hFdeg : ∀ q ∈ T, F q ∈ 𝒜 M := by
   271	    intro q hq
   272	    have h2 := SetLike.pow_mem_graded (M / m q) (hfdeg q hq)
   273	    rwa [smul_eq_mul, Nat.div_mul_cancel (Finset.dvd_prod_of_mem m hq)] at h2
   274	  have hFI : ∀ q ∈ T, F q ∈ I := fun q hq =>
   275	    Ideal.pow_mem_of_mem I (hfI q hq) _ (hquot q hq)
   276	  have hFin : ∀ q ∈ T, ∀ q' ∈ T.erase q, F q ∈ q' := fun q hq q' hq' =>
   277	    Ideal.pow_mem_of_mem _ (hfin q hq q' hq') _ (hquot q hq)
   278	  have hFout : ∀ q ∈ T, F q ∉ q := fun q hq hmem =>
   279	    hfout q hq ((hp q hq).mem_of_pow_mem _ hmem)
   280	  refine ⟨M, ∑ q ∈ T, F q, hMpos, sum_mem hFdeg,
   281	    Ideal.sum_mem _ fun q hq => hFI q hq, ?_⟩
   282	  intro q hq hmem
   283	  rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase T F hq] at hmem
   284	  have hrest : (∑ q' ∈ T.erase q, F q') ∈ q :=
   285	    Ideal.sum_mem _ fun q' hq' => hFin q' (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hq') q
   286	      (Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨(Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hq').symm, hq⟩)
   287	  exact hFout q hq ((Ideal.add_mem_iff_left _ hrest).mp hmem)

   289	/-- **Graded prime avoidance, general form** — the incomparability hypothesis of
   290	`exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem_of_antichain` removed.
   291	
   292	Any finite family of ideals is dominated by its **maximal** members, and avoiding
   293	those avoids all of them: if `f ∉ q` and `q' ≤ q` then `f ∉ q'`, since `f ∈ q'` would
   294	put `f` in `q`. The maximal members form an antichain by construction, so the
   295	previous theorem applies to them.
   296	
   297	Note the direction. It is the *maximal* primes that must be avoided, not the minimal
   298	ones — the inclusion runs the useful way only for a superset. Reducing to minimal
   299	primes, which is the reflex from the ungraded theory, would prove nothing here. -/
   300	theorem exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem
   301	    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (p : ι → Ideal A)
   302	    (hp : ∀ i ∈ s, (p i).IsPrime) (hph : ∀ i ∈ s, (p i).IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
   303	    (hrel : ∀ i ∈ s, ¬ (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal ≤ p i)
   304	    {I : Ideal A} (hI : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜) (hIp : ∀ i ∈ s, ¬ I ≤ p i)
   305	    (hM : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ f ∈ I) :
   306	    ∃ (M : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < M ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 M ∧ f ∈ I ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, f ∉ p i := by
   307	  classical
   308	  set S : Finset (Ideal A) := s.image p with hS
   309	  set T : Finset (Ideal A) := S.filter (fun q => Maximal (fun x => x ∈ S) q) with hT
   310	  -- every member of `T` is one of the `p i`
   311	  have hTmem : ∀ q ∈ T, ∃ i ∈ s, q = p i := by
   312	    intro q hq
   313	    obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hq).1
   314	    exact ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩
   315	  -- every `p i` sits below some member of `T`
   316	  have hTdom : ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ q ∈ T, p i ≤ q := by
   317	    intro i hi
   318	    obtain ⟨q, hle, hmax⟩ := S.exists_le_maximal (Finset.mem_image_of_mem p hi)
   319	    exact ⟨q, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hmax.1, hmax⟩, hle⟩
   320	  obtain ⟨M, f, hMpos, hfdeg, hfI, hfout⟩ :=
   321	    exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem_of_antichain 𝒜 T
   322	      (fun q hq => by obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hTmem q hq; exact hp i hi)
   323	      (fun q hq => by obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hTmem q hq; exact hph i hi)
   324	      (fun q hq => by obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hTmem q hq; exact hrel i hi)
   325	      (fun q hq q' hq' hne hle =>
   326	        hne ((Finset.mem_filter.mp hq).2.eq_of_ge (Finset.mem_filter.mp hq').1 hle).symm)
   327	      hI (fun q hq => by obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hTmem q hq; exact hIp i hi) hM
   328	  refine ⟨M, f, hMpos, hfdeg, hfI, fun i hi hmem => ?_⟩
   329	  obtain ⟨q, hq, hle⟩ := hTdom i hi
   330	  exact hfout q hq (hle hmem)

   332	/-- **`Proj 𝒜` satisfies `FiniteInAffine`.** The geometric half of §1, and the first
   333	statement in the chain that is about a scheme.
   334	
   335	A point of `Proj 𝒜` *is* a relevant homogeneous prime, and "relevant" is literally the
   336	hypothesis `exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem` needs — the structure field
   337	`ProjectiveSpectrum.not_irrelevant_le` serves simultaneously as the relevance input

   341	`Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen`, whose `f ∈ 𝒜 m` and `0 < m` hypotheses are exactly what

   345	positive-degree homogeneous element exists) is derived from *any* point of `Proj 𝒜`,

   347	the finite generalisation of the argument mathlib runs one point at a time inside

   352	  intro s hs
   353	  lift s to Finset (Proj 𝒜) using hs with t ht

   356	  obtain ⟨M, f, hMpos, hfdeg, -, hfout⟩ :=
   357	    exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem 𝒜 t
   358	      (fun x => (x.asHomogeneousIdeal).toIdeal)
   359	      (fun x _ => x.isPrime)
   360	      (fun x _ => x.asHomogeneousIdeal.isHomogeneous)
   361	      (fun x _ => x.not_irrelevant_le)
   362	      (I := (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal)

   364	      (fun x _ => x.not_irrelevant_le)

   366	        obtain ⟨m, g, hm, hgdeg, -, -⟩ :=

   368	            (I := (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal)
   369	            (p := (x₀.asHomogeneousIdeal).toIdeal)

   378	/-! ## §2. Descent along affine morphisms and immersions
   379	
   380	The affine and closed-immersion cases are transport.  The open-immersion case
   381	uses the independent finite prime-avoidance result from `StableAffineCover`; all
   382	later results are factorization or packaging.

   385	/-- **`FiniteInAffine` descends along any affine morphism.**
   386	
   387	The preimage of an affine open under an affine morphism is an affine open
   388	(`IsAffineOpen.preimage`), and a finite set upstairs has a finite image downstairs.
   389	So the property propagates in the direction that is useful for embeddings: from the
   390	ambient space to a subscheme.

   392	This generalises the already-landed `Scheme.finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom`
   393	(`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`), which is the special case `Y = Spec k`: there
   394	the conclusion came from `X` being outright affine, whereas here `Y` need only satisfy
   395	`FiniteInAffine`; relative projective space supplies the important application.
   396	That is the whole reason this direction is worth having as a separate lemma. -/

   398	    (h : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
   399	  intro s hs
   400	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (f.base '' s) (hs.image _)
   401	  exact ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1, U.2.preimage f⟩, fun x hx => hU ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩⟩

   404	containing the finite image need not lie in the immersion range.  Finite prime
   405	avoidance shrinks it to a basic open that does; its pullback is affine and still
   406	contains the original finite set. -/
   407	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isOpenImmersion {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
   408	    [IsOpenImmersion f] (hY : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
   409	  classical
   410	  intro s hs
   411	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := hY (f.base '' s) (hs.image f.base)
   412	  letI : Fintype s := hs.fintype
   413	  obtain ⟨r, hr, hrle⟩ :=
   414	    AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite U.2
   415	      (fun x : s => f.base x)
   416	      (fun x => hU ⟨x, x.2, rfl⟩)
   417	      (fun x => Scheme.Hom.mem_opensRange.mpr ⟨(x : X), rfl⟩)
   418	  refine ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ Y.basicOpen r,
   419	    (U.2.basicOpen r).preimage_of_isOpenImmersion f hrle⟩, ?_⟩
   420	  intro x hx
   421	  change f.base x ∈ Y.basicOpen r
   422	  exact hr ⟨x, hx⟩
